subject: PE & Wellbeing
source: National Curriculum (Physical Education); UK Chief Medical Officers' physical activity guidelines. Drive PE folder reviewed (TSS Long-Term PE Plan: fitness, fair play, leadership, resilience) and adapted to at-home, no-equipment, no-contact lessons.

lessons.title: Warm-up and cool-down: why they matter
objectives: Explain why we warm up and cool down
Perform a warm-up that raises heart rate and mobilises joints
Perform a safe cool-down with stretches

keywords.def: gentle exercise before activity to prepare the body
gentle exercise after activity to help the body recover
to move joints gently through their range
the beat of the heart you can feel at your wrist

starter: Bismillah. Name two ways to move safely.
What happens to your heart when you exercise?

teach.heading: Safety first
bullets: Wear comfortable clothing and non-slip footwear
Stop if you feel pain, dizziness or breathlessness
teach.note: Read this slide aloud every lesson. Parents are asked to confirm their child is well enough to take part and to tell the school about any medical condition (e.g. asthma: inhaler within reach). No contact activities in any TGA online PE lesson.

teach.heading: Why warm up?
teach.note: Ask pupils to rub hands together to feel warmth. Compare with cold elastic. Misconception: warming up is optional.

teach.heading: A three-part warm-up
bullets: Pulse raiser: march, jog on the spot
Stretches: calves and arms, short holds
teach.note: Lead each part for 2 minutes. Counting aloud helps keep pace.

teach.heading: Cool-down
teach.note: Cool-down helps heart rate return to normal. Do not bounce in stretches.

teach.heading: Plan your own
teach.note: Pupils write their plan. Teacher checks for safe choices.

practice: Show me a safe stretch for your arms.
independent: Do a one-minute pulse raiser and a one-minute mobiliser.
Hold two stretches for ten seconds each.
exit: Write and perform a six-move warm-up.
Add a cool-down of three stretches.
homework: Give two reasons to warm up.
Name one thing in a cool-down.
lessons.send: Lead a warm-up for your family and ask for feedback.

lessons.title: Core strength: tummy and back muscles
objectives: Perform safe core exercises with good technique

keywords.def: the muscles in your tummy, back and sides that keep you steady
holding your body straight, supported by arms and toes or knees
lifting hips from the floor while lying on your back
the correct way to do an exercise

starter: Name a stretch you can do.

teach.heading: Safety first
bullets: A mat, rug or soft carpet
Stop if you feel pain in your back
teach.note: Read this slide aloud every lesson. Parents are asked to confirm their child is well enough to take part and to tell the school about any medical condition (e.g. asthma: inhaler within reach). No contact activities in any TGA online PE lesson.

teach.heading: What is the core?
teach.note: Point to the area. Show a plank. Misconception: the core is only the 'six-pack'; it includes back and sides.

teach.heading: Kneeling plank
teach.note: Model alignment. Check for no sagging hips. Offer a wall plank as an easier option.

teach.heading: Glute bridge
bullets: Lie on back with knees bent
teach.note: Feet flat. Do 8 slow repetitions. Look for a straight line from shoulders to knees.

teach.heading: Superman hold
teach.note: Only lift a little. Stop if the back is uncomfortable.

independent: Hold a kneeling plank for 10 seconds, rest, and repeat.
Do 8 glute bridges with slow control.
exit: Complete a circuit: plank, bridge, superman, each for 20 seconds.
Note which is easiest and hardest.
homework: What should your back look like in a plank?
lessons.send: Do the three core exercises twice this week and record how it felt.
